limitations: No network access permitted, so declared dependency versions could not be checked against currently-published npm release lines; only internal consistency (lockfile, manifests, actual imports) was verified.
.npmrc was flagged as a secret file during indexing; its purpose (legacy-peer-deps) was confirmed without quoting its full contents.

jCodeMunch search_text reported one uncommitted change (src/components/landing/FAQSection.tsx) inside scanned scope not yet reflected in the index at query time; that file is unrelated to stack findings but index-derived absence results for it would be unreliable.

Package-manager commands (npm install/ls, tsc --noEmit) were not run per read-only rules, so unused/undeclared dependency claims rely on grep plus jCodeMunch search_text corroboration and direct source reading, not a resolver or type-checker.

findings.title: Two independently-maintained backend entrypoints (api/index.ts vs server/src) duplicate auth+DB wiring and have already drifted

identity.assertion: api/index.ts hand-rolls its own Node http handler, better-auth instance, and a copy of the Drizzle schema, duplicating server/src/index.ts (a Hono app) plus server/src/auth.ts and server/src/db/schema.ts; the two schema copies have already diverged.

evidence.detail: rewrites route all /api/(.*) traffic to /api, i.e. to api/index.ts — this is the only backend Vercel production deployments execute.
Defines its own pgTable('user'/'session'/'account'/'verification'/'projects', ...) and its own betterAuth(...) instance inline, instead of importing server/src/db/schema.ts or server/src/auth.ts.
The canonical schema (referenced by drizzle.config.ts) defines a clientProfiles table and a projects.clientProfileId column that api/index.ts's inline copy of the projects table omits entirely.
Only implements /api/health and /api/auth/** — the /api/projects GET/POST routes that exist in server/src/index.ts are absent from the Vercel-deployed handler.
Hono app defines app.get('/api/projects', ...) and app.post('/api/projects', ...) against the canonical schema; only reachable via `npm run server:dev` (tsx), not via the Vercel deployment path.
drizzle-kit schema/migrations are generated from ./server/src/db/schema.ts only, so any drizzle migration will not reflect the separate copy embedded in api/index.ts.

verification.note: Same independent verification as architecture-001 (shared underlying fact): api/index.ts is the sole Vercel production entry, does not implement /api/projects, and server/src/index.ts never runs in that deployment.

findings.title: Three AI provider SDKs are declared dependencies but the app calls those providers via raw fetch instead

identity.assertion: @anthropic-ai/sdk, @google/generative-ai, and openai are listed in dependencies, but no source file imports any of them; src/lib/ai/llm-client.ts talks to all three providers with hand-written fetch() calls to their REST endpoints.

evidence.detail: Anthropic path uses fetch('https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages', ...) directly instead of the @anthropic-ai/sdk client.
Gemini path uses fetch(`https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/${model}:generateContent...`) directly instead of @google/generative-ai.

findings.title: better-sqlite3 and its @types package are declared devDependencies but the app's only database driver is postgres/drizzle-orm/postgres-js

identity.assertion: devDependencies list better-sqlite3 and @types/better-sqlite3, but no file in server/, api/, electron/, or scripts/ imports better-sqlite3; the only Drizzle driver in use is drizzle-orm/postgres-js.

evidence.detail: Database client is `postgres(connectionString, ...)` from the `postgres` package, wired into `drizzle(client, { schema })` from drizzle-orm/postgres-js — no sqlite driver is instantiated anywhere.

findings.title: colorthief dependency is declared but never imported; palette extraction is implemented independently

identity.assertion: "colorthief": "^2.6.0" is a declared dependency with zero import sites in source; src/lib/palette/color-extractor.ts (the module whose name suggests it would use it) has no imports at all.

evidence.detail: File implements its own color-extraction logic with no import statements referencing colorthief or any other palette library.

verification.note: grep across src/electron/scripts and a jCodeMunch search_text pass over the indexed repo both found colorthief only in package.json, agreeing across two differently-shaped queries plus a direct read of the one plausible consumer file.

findings.title: Vercel's buildCommand skips the TypeScript typecheck and icon-generation steps that the project's own npm build script performs

identity.assertion: vercel.json's buildCommand is the bare "vite build", while package.json's "build" script is "node scripts/generate-icons.js && tsc && vite build" — Vercel deploys skip the tsc typecheck gate and the sharp-based icon regeneration that local/CI builds run.

evidence.detail: "buildCommand": "vite build", "framework": "vite" — no tsc step, no scripts/generate-icons.js step.
"build": "node scripts/generate-icons.js && tsc && vite build" is the script actually documented for local/manual builds.

findings.title: .npmrc forces legacy-peer-deps, indicating unresolved peer-dependency conflicts among declared packages

identity.assertion: .npmrc sets legacy-peer-deps=true, which suppresses npm's peer-dependency resolution errors; this is typically needed when some declared dependency's peerDependencies range doesn't accept the installed major versions (e.g. React 19) actually in use.

evidence.detail: File sets the legacy-peer-deps npm config flag (contents not quoted per secret-file handling instructions).
react/react-dom are pinned to ^19.0.0, a recent major version that some older-generation peerDependencies ranges in the dependency tree may not yet declare support for.

verification.note: No network/registry access was available to enumerate exactly which package's peerDependencies range triggers the conflict, so this is reported at low confidence as a signal rather than a pinpointed incompatibility.
